answer.generated: Vertical partitioning in distributed databases generates entities with fewer attributes, allowing them to be efficiently retrieved with a single access. In contrast, horizontal partitioning distributes data across multiple tables or partitions based on attribute values, potentially requiring joins to retrieve related data. While both partitioning techniques improve scalability, vertical partitioning simplifies query execution by reducing the number of columns accessed per row, whereas horizontal partitioning balances load but may complicate joins.
